• Frustum Culling. Given a specified camera pose, this step determines which 3D Gaussians are outside the camera’s
frustum. By doing so, 3D Gaussians outside the given view will not be involved in the subsequent computation.
• Splatting (Fig. 2a). In this step, 3D Gaussians (ellipsoids) in 3D space are projected into 2D image space (ellipses). The
projection proceeds through two transformations: first, transforming 3D Gaussians from world coordinates to camera
coordinates using viewing transformation, and subsequently splatting these Gaussians into 2D image space via an
approximation of projective transformation.
